reader_issues: Two parallel sets of notes are supplied (`chemistry-module-1..4` and `chemistry-ece-module-1..4`). While `chemistry-module-1..4` is complete, rigorous, and fully aligned with GXCYT122, `chemistry-ece-module-1..4` is an unpolished draft with missing syllabus topics and scientific errors.

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 7), the H2-O2 fuel cell is taught using an alkaline electrolyte (25% KOH or NaOH) with hydroxide-ion half-reactions, violating the official syllabus specification of 'H2-O2 fuel cell (acid electrolyte only)'.

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 9), under 'Electroless Plating of Copper', the 'Overall reaction' is erroneously given as the nickel-hypophosphite reaction: Ni2+ + H2PO2- + H2O -> Ni + H2PO3- + 2H+.

In `chemistry-ece-module-4`, the entire final section of the Module 4 syllabus (E-Waste, recycle/recovery/reuse, Chemistry of climate change, Greenhouse Gases, Ozone Depletion, and Sustainable Development Goals) is completely missing.

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 4), the solved numerical problems for the Nernst equation cover single electrodes, electrical energy, and equilibrium constants, but omit non-standard full-cell EMF calculations.

In `chemistry-ece-module-4` (page 3), Problem 2 has an error in the table where the ion is written as 'HCO3-' with a molecular weight of '122' (which is the mass of two HCO3- ions, whereas the single ion mass is 61), and the final subtraction '(104.17 + 50) - (122.95)' is left unevaluated.
In `chemistry-ece-module-3` (page 7), there is a LaTeX typo in the dielectric loss symbol: `(\'\varepsilon'')`.

coverage.topic: Disadvantages of Divide and Conquer Approach

reader_issues: Two parallel sets of notes exist in the repository: `chemistry-module-1..4` (comprehensive, rigorously edited, covering 100% of the GXCYT122 syllabus) and `chemistry-ece-module-1..4` (an older/unrefined track with missing topics and chemical errors).

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 7), the H2-O2 fuel cell is taught using an alkaline electrolyte (25% KOH or NaOH), whereas the official syllabus explicitly specifies 'H2-O2 fuel cell (acid electrolyte only)'. (`chemistry-module-1` page 9 properly teaches the acid electrolyte fuel cell).

In `chemistry-ece-module-4`, the final four syllabus topics of Module 4 (E-Waste disposal/recycle/recovery/reuse, Chemistry of climate change & Greenhouse Gases, Ozone Depletion, and Sustainable Development & SDGs) are completely omitted. (`chemistry-module-4` pages 11-14 cover all of these thoroughly).

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 9), under 'Electroless Plating of Copper', the 'Overall reaction' is erroneously given for Nickel plating with hypophosphite (Ni2+ + H2PO2- + H2O -> Ni + H2PO3- + 2H+) instead of Copper with formaldehyde.
In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 4, Problem 1), there is a formula typo: 'P -> Pb2+ + 2e-' instead of 'Pb -> Pb2+ + 2e-'.

In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 5), the glass electrode is inaccurately classified as a 'secondary reference electrode' and 'internal reference electrode' rather than an ion-selective indicator electrode.
In `chemistry-ece-module-1` (page 7), '%' symbols are dropped in text: 'allows charging only up to 90 (x=0.9)', 'Expensive to manufacture 40 > Ni-Cd', '25 KOH', and 'efficient (75 )'.

In `chemistry-ece-module-2` (page 2), the sol-gel equation '2Al(OR)3 + 3H2O -> Al2O3 + 3ROH' is stoichiometrically unbalanced (requires 6ROH) and the text mistakenly calls the oxide product 'aluminium nanoparticles' instead of alumina (Al2O3) nanoparticles.
In `chemistry-ece-module-3` (page 7), there is a LaTeX typo `(\'\varepsilon'')` in item 7 of DETA instrumentation.

In `chemistry-ece-module-4` (page 3), the table and Problem 2 treat the molecular weight of single ion HCO3- as 122 (which is the mass of two HCO3- ions) when computing CaCO3 equivalents, instead of using the equivalent weight 61.
In `chemistry-ece-module-4` (page 5), there is an unrendered LaTeX command `(\text{HOCl})` outside math delimiters.
